In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CABG is the preferred strategy for revascularization of patients with AHF and multivessel disease, but PCI is an acceptable option in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥ 40% and single vessel disease or LVEF < 40% and two vessel disease.
CABG is the preferred revascularizing technique for patients with AHF and multi-vessel coronary artery disease.
the evidence for revascularization in acute heart failure is still limited.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of CABG in patients with AHF is safe, with good results in terms of clinical outcomes and quality of life.
CABG should be the preferred option for revascularization in the setting of AHF, especially in patients with severe left ventricular dysfunction.
CABG is superior to PCI for patients with acute ischemic heart failure and multivessel disease, especially when the left ventricular function is impaired.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of death is higher in patients who underwent CABG than in patients who underwent PCI, and this difference is more pronounced in patients with preserved ejection fraction.
patients with acute ischemic heart failure should be treated according to the severity of their symptoms.
we need a randomized clinical trial to compare the outcomes of patients with AHF and acute myocardial infarction who undergo CABG versus PCI.
